title: unifig configuration
description:
Declarative configuration for a UniFi Network application (the Controller). Point your editor at this schema from the top of unifig.yaml:

  # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liambeeton/unifig/main/schema/unifig.schema.json

Any string value may contain ${ENV_VAR} references, which unifig replaces from the environment when it loads the file. Connection details (Controller host, API key) are not configured here — they live in the environment.

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: LAN networks and VLANs. Matched against the Controller by name; WAN slots are not networks and are configured separately.

wlans.title: WLANs
wlans.description: Wireless networks (SSIDs). Matched against the Controller by name, and each bound to the network its clients join.

zones.title: Firewall zones
zones.description: Zones in the Controller's zone-based firewall — named groups of networks that firewall policies govern the traffic between. Matched against the Controller by name. The Controller's own built-in zones (External, Internal, …) can be named here and managed like any other, but unifig never creates or deletes one.

firewall-policies.title: Firewall policies
firewall-policies.description: The rules governing traffic between a pair of zones. Matched against the Controller by name, and applied after the zones they name, so a file declaring a zone and a policy on it applies in one run.

port-forwards.title: Port forwards
port-forwards.description: Rules sending traffic that arrives on a port of the internet side to an address and port inside the network. Matched against the Controller by name. This section is the record of what the network exposes, so every field but `source` is required: a forward that did not say which port, which host and which protocol would not describe an exposed service.

wan.title: WAN slots
wan.description: The Controller's internet uplinks. These are Settings, not Resources: the Controller has a fixed set of WAN slots, so unifig only ever updates one — it never creates, deletes or prunes a slot, and a slot this file leaves out is one it does not manage.

encrypted-dns.title: Encrypted DNS
encrypted-dns.description: The Controller's Encrypted DNS setting, which UniFi's UI calls DNS Shield. A Setting like the WAN slots, and a singleton: a Controller has exactly one, so unifig only ever updates it and this section is a mapping rather than a list. Omitting the section leaves encrypted DNS entirely alone.

network.title: Network
network.description: A LAN network or VLAN on the Controller.

name.title: Name
name.description: The network's name, as shown in the Controller. This is its natural key: unifig matches on it, so renaming a network here means replacing it.

vlan.title: VLAN ID
vlan.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID. Omit for an untagged network such as the default LAN.

subnet.title: Subnet
subnet.description: The gateway address and prefix length in CIDR notation, e.g. 10.20.0.1/24 — the Controller's own convention, so the host part is the gateway rather than the network address.

wlan.title: WLAN
wlan.description: A wireless network (SSID) and the network its clients join.

name.title: SSID
name.description: The broadcast SSID. This is the WLAN's natural key.

network.title: Network
network.description: The name of the network this WLAN's clients join. Must be the name of a network defined in this file.

passphrase.title: Passphrase
passphrase.description: The WPA passphrase clients join with, 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters (a 64-character one is read as a hex PSK). Write it as a ${ENV_VAR} reference rather than in the file: unifig replaces it from the environment as it loads, so the committed config carries no secret. Omit it to leave the WLAN's security to the Controller — and note that a WLAN unifig creates without one is an open network anyone in range can join.

zone.title: Zone
zone.description: A named group of networks in the zone-based firewall.

name.title: Name
name.description: The zone's name, as shown in the Controller. This is its natural key: unifig matches on it, so renaming a zone here means replacing it — unless it is one of the Controller's built-in zones, which unifig matches but never creates or deletes.

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: The names of the networks this zone holds, each of which must be a network defined in this file. Stating the key makes this list the zone's membership, so a network you stop naming here is one the next apply takes out of the zone — and the plan says so before it does. Omit the key entirely to leave the Controller's own membership alone; write `networks: []` to say the zone holds none.

firewallPolicy.title: Firewall policy
firewallPolicy.description: A rule governing the traffic between a pair of zones.

name.title: Name
name.description: The policy's name, as shown in the Controller. This is its natural key.

action.title: Action
action.description: What the policy does with the traffic it matches: allow it, block it silently, or reject it with an ICMP error the sender can see.

source.title: Source zone
source.description: The name of the zone the traffic comes from. It may be a zone defined in this file or one the Controller already has, including a built-in zone such as External — which is why naming a zone that exists nowhere is reported when unifig reads the Controller, listing the zones the site really has, rather than offline.

destination.title: Destination zone
destination.description: The name of the zone the traffic is going to, on the same terms as `source`.

portForward.title: Port forward
portForward.description: One exposed service: the port traffic arrives on from the internet, and the address and port inside the network it is sent to.

name.title: Name
name.description: The forward's name, as shown in the Controller. This is its natural key: unifig matches on it, so renaming a forward here means replacing it.

port.title: Port
port.description: The port traffic arrives on from the internet — what the Controller's UI calls Port. unifig models a single port: a forward the Controller holds as a range or a comma-separated list is one this file cannot describe, so export leaves it out and `--prune` never deletes it.

forward-ip.title: Forward IP
forward-ip.description: The address inside the network that traffic is sent to. It is an address rather than the name of a network in this file, because that is what the Controller stores — so nothing checks it against the rest of the config, and a host that has moved is a change to make here.

forward-port.title: Forward port
forward-port.description: The port on that address traffic is sent to, which need not be the port it arrived on. A single port, on the same terms as `port`.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: Which traffic the forward passes: tcp, udp, or tcp_udp for both — what UniFi's UI shows as TCP/UDP. There is no default, because a forward opened to more than the service behind it needs is exposure nobody asked for.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where traffic is allowed to come from — what the Controller's UI calls From: `any`, or an address, an address range (a-b), or a CIDR block, optionally prefixed with `!` to mean everything except it. Omit the key to leave the Controller's own choice alone; note that a forward unifig creates without one accepts traffic from anywhere on the internet, and the plan says so before it does.

wanSlot.title: WAN slot
wanSlot.description: One of the Controller's internet uplinks. Changing one can cut this site off the internet, so unifig confirms every WAN change on its own before applying it.

slot.title: Slot
slot.description: Which uplink this is, in the Controller's own terms: WAN is the primary one, WAN2 the secondary, WAN_LTE_FAILOVER the cellular backup. This is the slot's identity — unifig matches on it. Which slots exist is the router's answer rather than this schema's, so naming one it does not have is reported when unifig reads the Controller, listing the slots it really has.

type.title: Connection type
type.description: How this uplink connects: dhcp for an address from the ISP, pppoe for one that authenticates first, disabled for a slot that is not in use. Static addressing is not modelled yet, so a slot configured that way in the Controller is left to it — omit this field and unifig manages nothing about how the slot connects.

username.title: PPPoE username
username.description: The username the ISP issued, for a pppoe slot. No quotes or spaces — the Controller refuses them.

password.title: PPPoE password
password.description: The password the ISP issued, for a pppoe slot. Write it as a ${ENV_VAR} reference rather than in the file: unifig replaces it from the environment as it loads, so the committed config carries no secret. No quotes or spaces — the Controller refuses them.

encryptedDNS.title: Encrypted DNS
encryptedDNS.description: How the Controller resolves DNS over an encrypted transport.

state.title: State
state.description: Which encrypted resolvers the Controller uses: off for none, auto for the Controller's own choice, manual for the built-in providers picked in its UI, custom for the servers listed below. Omit it to leave the Controller's own choice alone. unifig does not model the built-in provider list, so `manual` says which mode to be in and leaves the choice of providers to the Controller's UI.

servers.title: Custom DNS servers
servers.description: The custom encrypted resolvers, each given as a DNS stamp. This is one field rather than a collection of Resources: stating it makes this list the Controller's list, so a server the file stops naming is one the next apply removes — and the plan says so before it does. Omit the key entirely to leave the Controller's servers alone; write `servers: []` to say there should be none.

dnsServer.title: Custom DNS server
dnsServer.description: One encrypted resolver, named and described by its DNS stamp.

name.title: Name
name.description: What to call this resolver in the Controller. It is the server's natural key within this section, so two servers cannot share one.

stamp.title: DNS Stamp
stamp.description: The resolver's DNS stamp — the single sdns:// string that carries its address, protocol and public key. A stamp for a private endpoint identifies the account it belongs to, so unifig treats every stamp as a secret: write it as a ${ENV_VAR} reference rather than in the file, and unifig replaces it from the environment as it loads.
